summary: Ensho Nasu specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Ryukoku University (attested 1996) under Esho Mikogami and later held a post there as a visiting researcher (attested 2007).

Enshu Kurumiya works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Yukio Sakamoto, Ensho Kanakura, and Yosho Nomura, completing his PhD at the Australian National University in 1974 under Jan Willem de Jong, and was a professor at Rissho University (attested 1981–1985).
Entai Tomomatsu was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Keio University around 1918–1922. He held a post at Taisho University and founded the Publishing Association of Abhidharmakosa-vyakhya.

Erberto Lo Bue worked in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He earned his PhD from SOAS University of London (~1976–1981) and held posts at the University of Milan (~1985–1996) and the University of Bologna (~2002–2016).

Eric David Mortensen is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned his PhD at Harvard University (attested 2003) under Leonard van der Kuijp, Michael Witzel, and Kimberley C. Patton. He also studied under Chongren, Xiaoxun, Zhiben, Xuewen He, and Xi Aniu.

Eric Haruki Swanson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He has held posts at Loyola Marymount University and at Stanford University, where he is attested as a Senior Visiting Scholar in 2026.
Eric Huntington is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under the doctoral supervision of Gary A. Tubb.

Eric J. Sharpe was a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at Hartley Victoria College, the University of Manchester, and Uppsala University (doctorate ~1962–1965). He held posts at Manchester, Lancaster, Uppsala, and the University of Sydney (1977–1996).

Eric M. Greene is a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar who earned his PhD from UC Berkeley in 2012 under Robert H. Sharf. He has held assistant (attested 2017) and associate (attested 2026) professorships in religious studies at Yale University.

Eric P. Hamp was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Amherst College and Harvard University (~1946–1954). He held academic posts at the University of Michigan and the University of Chicago (~1953–1991).

Eric Stephen Goodell is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned an MA at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and studied at the University of Virginia (attested 2012) under Paul Groner.

Erica Baffelli is a scholar of Japanology and religious studies who studied under Massimo Raveri. She held a post at the University of Otago (attested 2015) and has served at the University of Manchester (attested 2016; Professor in Japanese Studies attested 2026).
Erica Biagetti is an Indologist and linguist working in computational fields. She earned her PhD from the University of Pavia by 2021 and held a post there.

Erich Frauwallner was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna (1918–1921). He held various posts there, including professor (1955–1964), and founded the Wiener Zeitschrift für die Kunde Süd- und Ostasiens in 1957.

Erich Haenisch worked in Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Tibetology, studying under Wilhelm Grube at Humboldt University of Berlin. He held professorships at the universities of Leipzig (~1925–1932), Berlin (1913, 1920, 1932), and Munich (1927–1951).

Erich Heintel was a philosophy scholar who earned his doctorate (~1931–1936) and habilitation (1940) at the University of Vienna. He held professorships in philosophy at the University of Vienna from 1952 until 1982.

Erich Rudolf Jaensch worked in philosophy and other fields, studying at Breslau, Göttingen (PhD ~1904–1908), and Strasbourg. He held professorships at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (1912–1913) and the University of Marburg beginning in 1913.

Erik Braun is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who completed his studies at Harvard University under Janet Gyatso. He held an affiliation at Harvard (attested 2010) and is a faculty member at the University of Virginia (attested 2026).

Erik Erikson studied at the University of Oxford and held academic posts at the University of California, Berkeley (~1939–1950), the University of Pittsburgh (~1951–1960), and Harvard University (~1960–1970).

Erik Haarh was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics who earned a doctorate at the University of Copenhagen (attested 1969). He held positions at the Royal Danish Library (1956, 1962) and served as a department head and professor at Aarhus University.
